card.name: Words after a noun in old prose
card.fires_on: Small linking or modifying words (in, into, little, depending, naturally) that come right after a noun or clause in older literary, historical or natural-history prose. They often sit where a prepositional phrase or participle is about to follow.

modes.label: Prepositions after a state
modes.description: A preposition such as in or into follows a verb or noun and starts a phrase of condition or place.
modes.example: where the Hussites were<< in>> open rebellion

modes.label: Participles and adverbs mid-clause
modes.description: A participle or adverb such as varying, depending or naturally opens an extra clause in 19th-century scientific writing.
modes.example: The process of diffusion would often be very slow,<< depending>> on climatal and geographical changes

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in old-fashioned book prose, just before a describing phrase continues.
